text:
**Short answer:** 30W is the minimum for a MacBook Air, and 70W or more is what you want for fast charging.

Apple says any USB-C charger that supports USB Power Delivery (USB PD) works, and you should use at least the wattage of the adapter Apple recommends for your model ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109509)). For MacBook Air models from 2022 or later, Apple lists these adapters:
- 30W (13-inch only)
- 35W dual USB-C
- 67W
- 70W

What comes in the box depends on the model:
- **M5 13-inch (2026):** a 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max, and it's fast-charge capable with a 70W or higher USB PD source ([Apple](https://support.apple.com/en-us/126320)).
- **M4 13-inch (2025):** a 30W adapter with the 8-core GPU, or a 35W dual-port adapter with the 10-core GPU. Fast charging needs the 70W adapter ([Apple](https://fd.xuwubk.eu.org/https/support.apple.com/en-us/122209)).

**Which to buy:**
- **Everyday charging:** 30W to 45W is enough, and the charger in the box already covers it.
- **Fast charging, or one charger for a laptop plus a phone:** choose 70W or higher. A 65W charger charges the laptop fine but is just under Apple's fast-charge threshold.

One option from the search results is the [Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W 2-pack](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u) at $49.99. It gives 65W from one USB-C port, but the laptop gets only 45W when several ports are in use. That page says its records don't include Apple's official wattage figure, and the link is an affiliate link (the site gets paid if you buy). You'd need a USB-C to USB-C cable, since this charger doesn't include the MagSafe cable.

If you tell me your model (13" or 15", and year), I can narrow this down. Apple's page also explains how to identify your MacBook Air.
